item.title: Composition and Empirical Formulas of Two Sulfur Oxides
item.stimulus:
A chemist analyzes three samples. Each sample is a pure compound that contains only sulfur and oxygen. The masses of sulfur and oxygen in each sample are listed below. Use the molar masses S = 32.06 g/mol and O = 16.00 g/mol.

Sample | Mass of sulfur (g) | Mass of oxygen (g)
1 | 1.603 | 1.600
2 | 0.6412 | 0.6400
3 | 0.8015 | 1.200

Answer the following.

parts.prompt: Calculate the percent by mass of sulfur in sample 1.

criteria.text: Calculates 50.05% sulfur by mass in sample 1.
criteria.evidence: Response divides the mass of sulfur by the total mass of sample 1 (1.603 g ÷ 3.203 g) and reports 50.05%.
criteria.fix: Add the masses of all the elements to get the sample mass, divide the element's mass by it, and multiply by 100.

parts.prompt: Determine the empirical formula of the compound in sample 1. Show the work that supports your answer.

criteria.text: Determines the empirical formula SO₂ from a 1 : 2 ratio of sulfur atoms to oxygen atoms.
criteria.evidence: Response converts the masses to amounts (0.05000 mol S and 0.1000 mol O) or uses an equivalent ratio calculation, shows that the S : O atom ratio is 1 : 2, and writes SO₂.
criteria.fix: Convert each element's mass to moles with its molar mass, then express the mole ratio as the lowest whole numbers.

parts.prompt: Do the data support the claim that sample 2 is the same compound as sample 1? Justify your answer using the law of definite proportions.

criteria.text: Answers yes: sample 2 has the same composition as sample 1 (50.05% S by mass, or 0.9981 g O per 1 g S, or a 1 : 2 S : O atom ratio), which is what the law of definite proportions requires for samples of one compound.
criteria.evidence: Response shows that sample 2 has the same composition as sample 1, either by calculating a matching composition value (percent S, mass ratio or atom ratio) or by showing that both elemental masses scale by the same factor, and states that one compound always has the same mass ratio of its elements.
criteria.fix: Show the composition matches, by a matching value or by both masses scaling by one factor, then cite the law.

parts.prompt: Sample 3 is a different pure compound of sulfur and oxygen. Determine its empirical formula. Show the work that leads to your answer.

criteria.text: Determines the empirical formula SO₃ from a 1 : 3 ratio of sulfur atoms to oxygen atoms.
criteria.evidence: Response finds 0.02500 mol S and 0.07500 mol O (or an equivalent ratio calculation) and writes SO₃.
criteria.fix: Find the moles of each element, compare them as an atom ratio, and write that ratio as the lowest whole-number subscripts.

item.model_answer:
(a) Mass of sample 1 = 1.603 g + 1.600 g = 3.203 g. Percent S = (1.603 g ÷ 3.203 g) × 100% = 50.05% S.

(b) Moles of S = 1.603 g ÷ 32.06 g/mol = 0.05000 mol. Moles of O = 1.600 g ÷ 16.00 g/mol = 0.1000 mol. The ratio S : O = 0.05000 : 0.1000 = 1 : 2, so the empirical formula is SO₂.

(c) Yes. Percent S in sample 2 = 0.6412 g ÷ (0.6412 g + 0.6400 g) × 100% = 50.05%, the same as sample 1 (equivalently, both samples contain 0.9981 g O per 1 g S). According to the law of definite proportions, every pure sample of a given compound has the same mass ratio of its elements, so the data are consistent with sample 2 being the same compound as sample 1.

(d) Moles of S = 0.8015 g ÷ 32.06 g/mol = 0.02500 mol. Moles of O = 1.200 g ÷ 16.00 g/mol = 0.07500 mol. The ratio S : O = 1 : 3, so the empirical formula is SO₃.
item.verification_python:
from fractions import Fraction
S,O=32.06,16.00
s1,o1=1.603,1.600
s2,o2=0.6412,0.6400
s3,o3=0.8015,1.200
assert abs(s1+o1-3.203)<1e-9
pS1=s1/(s1+o1)*100
assert abs(pS1-50.05)<0.005
pS2=s2/(s2+o2)*100
assert abs(pS2-50.05)<0.005
assert abs(o1/s1-0.9981)<0.00005 and abs(o2/s2-0.9981)<0.00005
nS1,nO1=s1/S,o1/O
assert abs(nS1-0.05000)<1e-6 and abs(nO1-0.1000)<1e-6
assert Fraction(nO1/nS1).limit_denominator(10)==2
nS3,nO3=s3/S,o3/O
assert abs(nS3-0.02500)<1e-6 and abs(nO3-0.07500)<1e-6
assert Fraction(nO3/nS3).limit_denominator(10)==3
assert abs((s2/S)/(o2/O)-0.5)<1e-6
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Empirical Formula and Definite Proportions of an Iron Oxide
item.stimulus:
A student analyzes two samples of a red-brown solid that is a pure compound containing only iron and oxygen. Each sample is collected from a different supplier. For each sample, the masses of iron and oxygen are determined. The results are shown below.

Sample | Mass of sample (g) | Mass of Fe (g) | Mass of O (g)
1 | 2.500 | 1.749 | 0.751
2 | 4.000 | 2.798 | 1.202

Use molar masses Fe = 55.85 g/mol and O = 16.00 g/mol.
item.model_answer:
(a) Percent Fe = (1.749 g ÷ 2.500 g) × 100 = 69.96% Fe.

(b) mol Fe = 1.749 g ÷ 55.85 g/mol = 0.03132 mol Fe. mol O = 0.751 g ÷ 16.00 g/mol = 0.0469 mol O. Dividing by the smaller amount: Fe = 0.03132/0.03132 = 1.00; O = 0.0469/0.03132 = 1.50. Multiplying both by 2 gives Fe:O = 2:3, so the empirical formula is Fe2O3.

(c) Sample 2: percent Fe = (2.798 g ÷ 4.000 g) × 100 = 69.95% Fe, essentially identical to 69.96% for Sample 1. (Equivalently, the Fe:O mass ratio is 2.798/1.202 = 2.33 for Sample 2 and 1.749/0.751 = 2.33 for Sample 1.) Because the composition by mass is the same within measurement precision, the data are consistent with both samples being the same compound, as required by the law of definite proportions. The classmate's claim is not supported.

(d) In the compound, Fe and O are always combined in the fixed ratio of 2 Fe to 3 O in every formula unit. Each Fe atom and each O atom has a characteristic average mass, so the mass of Fe per formula unit to mass of O per formula unit is always (2 × 55.85)/(3 × 16.00) = 2.33. A larger sample simply contains more formula units, which multiplies both masses by the same factor, so the mass ratio does not change.
item.verification_python:
import math
Fe=55.85; O=16.00
m1,fe1,o1=2.500,1.749,0.751
m2,fe2,o2=4.000,2.798,1.202
assert abs(fe1+o1-m1)<1e-9 and abs(fe2+o2-m2)<1e-9
p1=fe1/m1*100
assert round(p1,2)==69.96
nFe=fe1/Fe; nO=o1/O
assert abs(nFe-0.03132)<5e-6
assert abs(nO-0.0469)<5e-5
r=nO/nFe
assert abs(r-1.50)<0.01
assert round(r*2)==3
p2=fe2/m2*100
assert round(p2,2)==69.95
r1=fe1/o1; r2=fe2/o2
assert round(r1,2)==2.33 and round(r2,2)==2.33
assert round(r2,3)==2.328
th=(2*Fe)/(3*O)
assert round(th,3)==2.327 and round(th,2)==2.33
assert abs(2*Fe/(2*Fe+3*O)*100-69.94)<0.01
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Iron Oxide Composition and the Law of Definite Proportions
item.stimulus:
A student analyzes samples of a pure solid compound that contains only iron and oxygen. Samples 1 and 2 are taken from the same reagent bottle. Sample 3 is a dark solid from a different bottle that also contains only iron and oxygen. For each sample, the student determines the total mass of the sample and the mass of iron it contains. The mass of oxygen is found by difference. Use molar masses Fe = 55.85 g/mol and O = 16.00 g/mol.

Sample | Mass of sample (g) | Mass of Fe (g) | Mass of O (g)
1 | 2.000 | 1.399 | 0.601
2 | 5.000 | 3.497 | 1.503
3 | 3.000 | 2.171 | 0.829
item.model_answer:
(a) Sample 1: (1.399 g / 2.000 g) × 100 = 69.95% Fe. Sample 2: (3.497 g / 5.000 g) × 100 = 69.94% Fe. The two samples differ in mass, yet they have the same percent iron within measurement precision. The law of definite proportions says that every pure sample of a compound has the same mass ratio of its elements, and these results match that.

(b) The moles of each element are:
n(Fe) = 1.399 g ÷ 55.85 g/mol = 0.02505 mol
n(O) = 0.601 g ÷ 16.00 g/mol = 0.0376 mol
Dividing each amount by 0.02505 mol gives Fe = 1.00 and O = 1.50. Multiplying both by 2 gives Fe 2 : O 3. The empirical formula is Fe2O3.

(c) Sample 3: (2.171 g / 3.000 g) × 100 = 72.37% Fe. This differs from the 69.9% Fe in Samples 1 and 2, so Sample 3 is not the same compound. A pure compound always has the same composition by mass. As a check, the moles in Sample 3 are 2.171/55.85 = 0.03887 mol Fe and 0.829/16.00 = 0.0518 mol O. This gives O:Fe = 1.33, which corresponds to Fe3O4.

(d) In Fe2O3, iron and oxygen are combined in a fixed proportion of 2 Fe for every 3 O in each formula unit. Every atom (ion) of a given element has the same characteristic average mass. A larger sample simply contains more formula units. As a result, the total masses of Fe and O increase in the same proportion, and the ratio of iron mass to oxygen mass stays constant for any sample size.
item.verification_python:

Fe=55.85;O=16.00
# data consistency
assert abs(2.000-1.399-0.601)<1e-9
assert abs(5.000-3.497-1.503)<1e-9
assert abs(3.000-2.171-0.829)<1e-9
p1=1.399/2.000*100;p2=3.497/5.000*100;p3=2.171/3.000*100
assert abs(p1-69.95)<0.005
assert abs(p2-69.94)<0.005
assert abs(p3-72.37)<0.005
# mass ratio Fe:O
assert abs(1.399/0.601-2.33)<0.01 and abs(3.497/1.503-2.33)<0.01
# theoretical Fe2O3 percent
th=2*Fe/(2*Fe+3*O)*100
assert abs(th-69.94)<0.01
nFe=1.399/Fe;nO=0.601/O
assert abs(nFe-0.02505)<0.000005
assert abs(nO-0.0376)<0.00005
assert abs(nO-0.03756)<0.000005
r=nO/nFe
assert abs(r-1.50)<0.005
assert round(r*2)==3
# sample 3
nFe3=2.171/Fe;nO3=0.829/O
assert abs(nFe3-0.03887)<0.000005
assert abs(nO3-0.0518)<0.00005
r3=nO3/nFe3
assert abs(r3-1.33)<0.005
assert round(r3*3)==4
th3=3*Fe/(3*Fe+4*O)*100
assert abs(th3-72.36)<0.01
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Empirical and Molecular Formula of an Organic Acid
item.stimulus:
A chemist isolates a white crystalline organic acid that contains only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. Two samples of the acid, obtained from different sources, are purified and analyzed to find the mass of each element they contain. The results are shown below.

Sample | Mass of sample (g) | Mass of C (g) | Mass of H (g) | Mass of O (g)
A | 3.000 | 1.220 | 0.154 | 1.626
B | 5.000 | 2.034 | 0.256 | 2.710

In a separate experiment, the molar mass of the acid is found to be 118.1 g/mol. Use the molar masses C = 12.01 g/mol, H = 1.008 g/mol, and O = 16.00 g/mol.
item.model_answer:
(a) Mass ratio of C to O: sample A, 1.220 g / 1.626 g = 0.7503; sample B, 2.034 g / 2.710 g = 0.7506. Mass fraction of C: A, 1.220/3.000 = 0.4067; B, 2.034/5.000 = 0.4068. The ratios of the masses of the elements are the same in both samples (within measurement precision), which is what the law of definite proportions requires of any pure sample of one compound. The data are consistent with the claim.

(b) Moles in sample A:
C: 1.220 g / 12.01 g/mol = 0.1016 mol
H: 0.154 g / 1.008 g/mol = 0.153 mol
O: 1.626 g / 16.00 g/mol = 0.1016 mol
Divide by the smallest (0.1016): C = 1.00, H = 1.50, O = 1.00. Multiply by 2 to get whole numbers: C : H : O = 2 : 3 : 2. Empirical formula: C2H3O2.

(c) Empirical formula mass = 2(12.01) + 3(1.008) + 2(16.00) = 59.04 g/mol. 118.1 / 59.04 = 2.00. Molecular formula = (C2H3O2) × 2 = C4H6O4.

(d) Solid CaCl2 is not made of individual molecules. It is an extended array of Ca²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held together by electrostatic attractions in a fixed proportion of one Ca²⁺ for every two Cl⁻. Because there is no discrete particle with a definite number of atoms, the formula can only express the lowest whole-number ratio of ions, the formula unit CaCl2. The organic acid, by contrast, consists of discrete molecules each containing exactly 4 C, 6 H, and 4 O atoms, so it has a molecular formula that can be a whole-number multiple of its empirical formula.
item.verification_python:
from fractions import Fraction
C,H,O=12.01,1.008,16.00
A=(3.000,1.220,0.154,1.626)
B=(5.000,2.034,0.256,2.710)
assert abs(sum(A[1:])-A[0])<1e-9
assert abs(sum(B[1:])-B[0])<1e-9
rA=A[1]/A[3]; rB=B[1]/B[3]
assert abs(rA-0.7503)<1e-4 and abs(rB-0.7506)<1e-4
fA=A[1]/A[0]; fB=B[1]/B[0]
assert abs(fA-0.4067)<1e-4 and abs(fB-0.4068)<1e-4
assert abs(rA-rB)/rA<0.001

item.title: Composition and Empirical Formulas of Two Sulfur Oxides
item.stimulus:
A chemist analyzes three samples. Each sample is a pure compound that contains only sulfur and oxygen. The masses of sulfur and oxygen in each sample are listed below. Use the molar masses S = 32.06 g/mol and O = 16.00 g/mol.

Sample | Mass of sulfur (g) | Mass of oxygen (g)
1 | 1.603 | 1.600
2 | 0.6412 | 0.6400
3 | 0.8015 | 1.200

Answer the following.

parts.prompt: Calculate the percent by mass of sulfur in sample 1.

criteria.text: Calculates 50.05% sulfur by mass in sample 1.
criteria.evidence: Response divides the mass of sulfur by the total mass of sample 1 (1.603 g ÷ 3.203 g) and reports 50.05%.
criteria.fix: Add the masses of all the elements to get the sample mass, divide the element's mass by it, and multiply by 100.

parts.prompt: Determine the empirical formula of the compound in sample 1. Show the work that supports your answer.

criteria.text: Determines the empirical formula SO₂ from a 1 : 2 ratio of sulfur atoms to oxygen atoms.
criteria.evidence: Response converts the masses to amounts (0.05000 mol S and 0.1000 mol O) or uses an equivalent ratio calculation, shows that the S : O atom ratio is 1 : 2, and writes SO₂.
criteria.fix: Convert each element's mass to moles with its molar mass, then express the mole ratio as the lowest whole numbers.

parts.prompt: Do the data support the claim that sample 2 is the same compound as sample 1? Justify your answer using the law of definite proportions.

criteria.text: Answers yes: sample 2 has the same composition as sample 1 (50.05% S by mass, or 0.9981 g O per 1 g S, or a 1 : 2 S : O atom ratio), which is what the law of definite proportions requires for samples of one compound.
criteria.evidence: Response shows that sample 2 has the same composition as sample 1, either by calculating a matching composition value (percent S, mass ratio or atom ratio) or by showing that both elemental masses scale by the same factor, and states that one compound always has the same mass ratio of its elements.
criteria.fix: Show the composition matches, by a matching value or by both masses scaling by one factor, then cite the law.

parts.prompt: Sample 3 is a different pure compound of sulfur and oxygen. Determine its empirical formula. Show the work that leads to your answer.

criteria.text: Determines the empirical formula SO₃ from a 1 : 3 ratio of sulfur atoms to oxygen atoms.
criteria.evidence: Response finds 0.02500 mol S and 0.07500 mol O (or an equivalent ratio calculation) and writes SO₃.
criteria.fix: Find the moles of each element, compare them as an atom ratio, and write that ratio as the lowest whole-number subscripts.

item.model_answer:
(a) Mass of sample 1 = 1.603 g + 1.600 g = 3.203 g. Percent S = (1.603 g ÷ 3.203 g) × 100% = 50.05% S.

(b) Moles of S = 1.603 g ÷ 32.06 g/mol = 0.05000 mol. Moles of O = 1.600 g ÷ 16.00 g/mol = 0.1000 mol. The ratio S : O = 0.05000 : 0.1000 = 1 : 2, so the empirical formula is SO₂.

(c) Yes. Percent S in sample 2 = 0.6412 g ÷ (0.6412 g + 0.6400 g) × 100% = 50.05%, the same as sample 1 (equivalently, both samples contain 0.9981 g O per 1 g S). According to the law of definite proportions, every pure sample of a given compound has the same mass ratio of its elements, so the data are consistent with sample 2 being the same compound as sample 1.

(d) Moles of S = 0.8015 g ÷ 32.06 g/mol = 0.02500 mol. Moles of O = 1.200 g ÷ 16.00 g/mol = 0.07500 mol. The ratio S : O = 1 : 3, so the empirical formula is SO₃.
item.verification_python:
from fractions import Fraction
S,O=32.06,16.00
s1,o1=1.603,1.600
s2,o2=0.6412,0.6400
s3,o3=0.8015,1.200
assert abs(s1+o1-3.203)<1e-9
pS1=s1/(s1+o1)*100
assert abs(pS1-50.05)<0.005
pS2=s2/(s2+o2)*100
assert abs(pS2-50.05)<0.005
assert abs(o1/s1-0.9981)<0.00005 and abs(o2/s2-0.9981)<0.00005
nS1,nO1=s1/S,o1/O
assert abs(nS1-0.05000)<1e-6 and abs(nO1-0.1000)<1e-6
assert Fraction(nO1/nS1).limit_denominator(10)==2
nS3,nO3=s3/S,o3/O
assert abs(nS3-0.02500)<1e-6 and abs(nO3-0.07500)<1e-6
assert Fraction(nO3/nS3).limit_denominator(10)==3
assert abs((s2/S)/(o2/O)-0.5)<1e-6
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')
